name: deolekar-tabla
description: Real recorded tabla, tuned to C#, from the Zenodo tabla strokes dataset by Subodh Deolekar (CC BY 4.0). See LICENSE.txt.
notes: 1 of the stroke vocabulary are stand-ins, not recordings: ki plays ka. See each entry's `notes` and README.md.

na.notes: Only 11 of the dataset's 50 `Na` takes are free of digital clipping; the round robins here are drawn from those.

te.notes: Dataset class `T`, read as the damped syahi stroke. VERIFY by ear.

re.notes: Dataset class `Tr` (tra/tre), promoted to `re`. Measured against every other class it is the shortest (63ms mean vs 109ms for `T`) and the quietest dayan stroke (peak 0.20 vs 0.56), while sitting spectrally in the closed-dayan family (cosine 0.84 to `Ti`, 0.80 to `T`). That is the profile data/strokes.yaml describes for `re`: a closed ring-finger flick with the least energy of any stroke. Not labelled `re` by the dataset, so VERIFY by ear -- but it is real recorded material of roughly the right gesture, which the previous `re`->`te` alias was not.

ki.notes: The dataset has no separate `ki`. Probably correct rather than a compromise -- data/strokes.yaml notes `ki` is commonly the same physical closed-bayan stroke as `ka`. VERIFY.

dha.notes: Real recorded `Dha` -- bayan and dayan struck together, not a mix of two one-shots. 86% of its energy sits below 200Hz, so the bayan is genuinely there. VERIFY by ear which dayan stroke is in it: measurement does not settle that question here, because over 250Hz-8kHz it scores 0.46-0.63 against every candidate (`T`, `Tin`, `Na`, `Ti`, `Ta`) with no clear winner. Treat the dataset's own label as the best evidence available and your ear as better than both.

dhun.notes: VERIFY -- inferred, not labelled. The dataset class is `Da`, which is ambiguous, but its dayan component matches `Tu` (cosine 0.76) and its bayan content is strong, so acoustically it is ge+tun = dhun. If it is really a `daa` to your ear, delete this entry.
